Septic Alarms

Inspecting Your Septic ALERT System

Septic alarms are critical early warning devices designed to alert homeowners to potential problems within their septic systems. These advanced monitoring tools continuously assess key aspects of your septic system’s operation, including water levels, pump function, and electrical components. When irregularities are detected, such as abnormally high water levels or pump malfunctions, the alarm immediately notifies you through audible and visual signals. This early detection allows for prompt intervention, preventing minor issues from escalating into major failures that could lead to system backups, environmental contamination, or expensive repairs. By integrating a septic alarm into your system, you’re taking a proactive step in maintaining your septic system’s health and avoiding unexpected emergencies.

1. Alarm Activation

When your septic alarm sounds, it indicates a potential issue in your system. Remain calm and avoid using water until the problem is resolved.

2. Initial Assessment

While waiting for our arrival, check the alarm panel for any specific error codes or lights if it’s safe to do so. This information will help us when we’re on-site.

3. Water Usage

We strongly recommend reducing water usage in your home until we’ve addressed the issue on-site. This means avoiding showers, laundry, dishwashing, and limiting toilet flushing

4. Visual Inspection

If possible, visually inspect the area around your septic tank and drain field from a safe distance. Note any signs of overflow, unusual odors, or wet spots to report to our technicians upon arrival.

5. Contact Us

Call our 24/7 emergency service line immediately. We’ll dispatch a team to your location promptly. Provide us with your observations to help us prepare for the on-site visit.

6. On-Site Evaluation:

Once on-site, our skilled technicians will conduct a thorough assessment of your system.

Septic Alarm FAQ

What is a septic alarm and why do I need one?

We install septic alarms to alert you to potential issues in your septic system. These devices monitor water levels and pump function, warning you of problems before they escalate into costly emergencies. We consider them essential for maintaining your system’s health and avoiding unexpected failures.

How does a septic alarm work?

Our septic alarms use float switches inside your tank to detect abnormal water levels. When levels rise too high, the alarm triggers, activating both audible and visual alerts. We set them up to give you ample time to contact us for on-site service before a serious problem develops.

What should I do when my septic alarm goes off?

When your alarm sounds, we advise reducing water usage immediately and contacting our 24/7 emergency line. Our team will quickly dispatch to your location for an on-site assessment and resolution. Remember, the alarm is a warning system – it’s crucial to act promptly when it activates.

How often should septic alarms be tested?

We recommend testing your septic alarm monthly to ensure it’s functioning correctly. During our routine on-site maintenance visits, we always include a thorough check and test of your alarm system as part of our comprehensive service.

Can you install a septic alarm on my existing system?

Absolutely! We can retrofit most existing septic systems with an alarm. During an on-site visit, our technicians will assess your current setup and recommend the most suitable alarm system for your specific needs. It’s a smart upgrade that we often suggest to our clients for added peace of mind.
